newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TWO LEAKS AT S.AFRICAN NUCLEAR POWER STATION.
newsitem.headline: TWO LEAKS AT S.AFRICAN NUCLEAR POWER STATION.

text.p: Accidental leaks at South African electricity generator Eskom's Koeberg power have twice this year exposed workers to radiation, the parliamentary minerals and energy committee heard on Wednesday.
University of Cape Town Science Advice Unit director Thomas Auf der Heyde told the committee that the incidents took place in early March and May.
"In the first case the exposure was below the levels set by the Council for Nuclear Safety but higher than the in-house limits that Eskom set for itself," he said.
The CNS limit is 50 millisieverts (mSv) a year while that of Eskom is 20 mSv.
"In the second case, the exposure that was suffered was approximately double the annual limit that the CNS sets," Auf der Heyde said.
The committee is planning a trip to Koeberg, in Western Cape province, on June 6 and Auf der Heyde had been asked to brief it on the nuclear industry.

In the first case, a worker went into an area which was off-limits. "Whether he disregarded the fact that he was off-limits or whether signs were not properly placed, I do not know," Auf der Heyde said.

"In the second case, which involved three workers, it seems that one of the pieces of equipment that the workers were using to monitor the radiation that they were exposed to was defective and therefore they were not aware of the fact that they were being exposed to higher levels than they ought to be."
The radiation associated with the equipment that they were servicing would ordinarily be very low.
A CNS report on the second incident said that steps had been taken to tighten up controls on testing equipment and make workers more aware of the need for safety procedures.

"Although two of the three individuals involved in the incident have received radiation exposures in excess of the annual limit prescribed ny the CNS, it has been concluded that no licence conditions were violated," the report said.
"Therefore no legal action against Eskom is recommended."
